scope: Pinned Icarus future read-write synchronization supports an explicit digital event ordering; not CPU synchronization or physical timing.

checked_source.finding: sync_cb marks non-read-only synchronized callbacks as writable; make_sync uses supplied relative time and schedules sync=true/readonly=false.
At a given timestamp, active then inactive then NBA queues drain before rwsync. After rwsync creates more active/NBA work, the main scheduler loop drains that work before RO.

supported_contract: Schedule input application with cbReadWriteSynch at strictly positive requested-time minus current-time.
Already scheduled clock edges and their sequential delta updates settle before the input batch at the same timestamp.
New input-triggered active/NBA work settles before the complete RO observation.
Blocking reads and binary response writes remain confined to RO callbacks.
No extra picosecond, altered clock frequency, or CPU lookahead grant is implied.
required_actual_regression: Compare complete raw event time/kind/four-state timelines for unsplit Drive15001 and Advance12001 followed by Drive15001. Require old rising-edge sampling, preserved clock level/new phase and later input/reset sampling.
